title: Certified n=68 refinement: side 8.798795237221
body:
**Update:** The newer [v1.1.0 certificate](https://github.com/lollipoll/certified-square-packing-68/releases/tag/v1.1.0) proves **s(68) ≤ 8.798795237218283903** (rounded upward). See the update comment below for exact coordinates, checks, and attribution. The original submission below records the earlier v1.0.0 result.

Hi David,

I’d like to submit a certified refinement of the 68-unit-square packing for consideration for the Squares in Squares table.

The enclosing side is exactly:

**8.798795237221 = 8798795237221 / 1000000000000**

**Release and supporting audit:**
https://github.com/lollipoll/certified-square-packing-68/releases/tag/v1.0.0

This is a refinement of Jake Loyd’s published September 2026 construction, produced with assistance from OpenAI Codex through constrained numerical optimization followed by rational repair. The starting construction and its earlier contributors should retain their attribution.

**Exact verification**

The certificate stores rational centers and rational half-angle rotation parameters. Two separately implemented Python checkers confirm that all 68 squares have unit side length, lie inside the container, and have nonoverlapping interiors.

Both checkers use exact rational arithmetic with zero acceptance tolerance and check all **2,278 unordered pairs**. The minimum wall clearance and minimum pair separating margin are strictly positive. All 25 included verifier tests pass.

To reproduce the checks using Python 3.9 or newer:

```bash
git clone --branch v1.0.0 --depth 1 https://github.com/lollipoll/certified-square-packing-68.git
cd certified-square-packing-68
python3 check_hashes.py
python3 verify.py n68.json --n 68
python3 independent_support_check.py n68.json --n 68
python3 -m unittest discover -s . -p 'test_*.py' -v
```

No third-party Python packages or optimizer are required.

The authoritative `n68.json` certificate has SHA-256:

```text
00e402139c76663a4bac8dbaed8705d1b8a04ccfd32f2945065f70ade5d6eb19
```

**Comparison reviewed on October 7, 2026 (UTC)**

| Construction or posted claim | Enclosing side |
|---|---:|
| This exact certificate | **8.798795237221** |
| [franciscouzo’s posted coordinate-file header](https://github.com/franciscouzo/square-packing/blob/master/n68.txt) | 8.798795237222592 |
| [Kingbird’s listed packing](https://kingbird.myphotos.cc/packing/squares_in_squares.html) | 8.7987961402601 |

The certified side is smaller than franciscouzo’s posted value by **0.000000000001592**. I recognize that this is a very small refinement and does not establish a new packing arrangement or global optimality.

I also see the earlier pending submission in #2. Its public issue provides no side or coordinates, so I cannot determine whether it precedes or improves upon this bound.

Could you review this construction and let me know whether it qualifies for a table update, including whether any earlier submissions affect priority?

The release includes the supporting `independent-audit.zip`. The standalone certificate checks above are self-contained; the attached audit’s full-workflow replay additionally requires the separate original `candidate-export.zip`.

Thank you,
Seth Rehwaldt
